basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: Defines what money is (unit, instrument, amount), not accounts, balances or payments.
Separates the unit of account from the instrument that embodies value and from its issuer.
Tracks legal tender status and lifecycle, including redenomination and withdrawal.

may: Identify a currency or instrument and construct a valid amount.
Apply declared rounding and conversion rules with a stated rate source.
mustNot: Move or hold value; payments belong to the payment model.
Treat a withdrawn or non-legal-tender instrument as valid without checking its status.
Use an exchange rate without recording its source and time.
requiresHuman: Accepting an unusual instrument (for example a token) as settlement.
Choosing a rate source for a binding conversion.

considerations: Errors in money definitions propagate into what people pay and receive.
Instruments differ in risk to holders; presenting e-money or tokens as equal to central bank money can mislead.

owners.steward: Issuers and monetary authorities own units and instruments; the local record is a governed copy.

items: A monetary unit has an ISO 4217 code and minor unit; an instrument has an issuer, form and claim.
